# Accounting transport fixtures

`qbo.json` and `xero.json` are **authored synthetic protocol examples**, recorded in this repository on 17 October 2026. They are based on official endpoint schemas and examples. They are not captured account traffic, real exports, a real connection, or provider acceptance evidence. Every ID, contact, token, amount and document here is synthetic. The `.invalid` origins cannot address a live company. Nothing imports these files into application runtime.

Each file has `baseUrl`, synthetic `credentials`, and document cases for items, invoices, bills, balanced COGS journals and supplier-receipt attachments; QBO also covers credit memos, source-identified payments and unpaid invoice voids. A case contains its common `document`, `post` and `read` exchanges, and `expected.post` and `expected.read`. `read.document` includes the returned remote ID. Non-receipt cases additionally contain a `lookup` exchange without a remote ID, with the same expected result as `read`. Each exchange records `request.method`, `path`, optional decoded `query`, provider-specific headers and JSON, form or text body, plus `response.status` and `response.body`. Authentication headers are generated from fixture credentials; they are deliberately not duplicated in every exchange. `errors` contains revoked-authorization and rate-limit responses.

The transport seam is `config.fetch`; inject a fixture responder only in tests. Production code always calls the actual configured HTTP provider, propagates failures, and has no fixture, mock, retry or fallback path. These fixtures support deterministic protocol tests at the network edge, not claims that a ledger processed the documents.

## Interface and mappings

`src/pier/books/adapters/types.ts` exports `BookDocument`, `BookResult`, `BooksAdapter` (`post` and `read`) and `BooksAdapterConfig`. The factories are `createQboAdapter` in `qbo.ts` and `createXeroAdapter` in `xero.ts`. Supply the provider origin as `baseUrl`; QBO appends `/v3/company/{realmId}`, Xero appends `/api.xro/2.0`. QBO requires `credentials.accessToken` and `realmId`; Xero requires `accessToken` and `tenantId`. Tokens must already be authorized and current. The adapters do not acquire, persist or refresh OAuth credentials.

| Common kind | QBO create / read | Xero create / read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | `POST /item`; `GET /item/{Id}` or query `Item.Name` | `PUT /Items`; `GET /Items/{ItemID}` or filter `Code` |
| `invoice` | `POST /invoice`; `GET /invoice/{Id}` or query `Invoice.DocNumber` | `PUT /Invoices` with `ACCREC`; `GET /Invoices/{InvoiceID}` or filter number and type |
| `bill` | `POST /bill`; `GET /bill/{Id}` or query `Bill.DocNumber` | `PUT /Invoices` with `ACCPAY`; `GET /Invoices/{InvoiceID}` or filter number and type |
| `journal` | `POST /journalentry`; `GET /journalentry/{Id}` or query `JournalEntry.DocNumber` | `PUT /ManualJournals` with `POSTED`; `GET /ManualJournals/{ManualJournalID}` or filter narration |
| `receipt` | Multipart `POST /upload` linked to a Bill; query its Attachables | Raw UTF-8 `PUT /Invoices/{billID}/Attachments/{name}`; `GET` that bill's Attachments |

Account and party references must be owner-mapped provider identifiers, never local IDs assumed to be provider IDs. `line.account` means QBO account ID or Xero account code; `line.itemId` means QBO item ID or Xero item code. QBO invoice lines require mapped non-inventory items and a unit price. Xero invoice and bill lines require a unit price. Item documents contain exactly one definition line: its account is the sales income account and its description is the name and description. QBO transaction references must fit its 21-character DocNumber limit; Xero item codes allow 30 characters and names allow 50. Oversize references require explicit mapping, never truncation.

Items are deliberately **non-inventory or untracked** in both ledgers. QBO bills use account-based asset or expense lines. Pier owns physical quantities and sends separately balanced journals, avoiding a second inventory and cost of goods posting from ledger-tracked items. The shared document currently has no purchase-details account pair, tax mapping, FX or provider-tax mapping. QBO additionally supports linked customer credits, source-identified cash allocations and unpaid voids. Consequently this transport subset supports USD documents with **no tax**, sellable item definitions and explicit balanced journals; it does not implement the whole ACCOUNT-001 and ACCOUNT-002 contract. Xero uses `NoTax`; QBO sales lines use `NON`. Taxable transactions require an extended explicit mapping before enablement. An untracked item is not a ledger inventory valuation snapshot.

All outgoing money is validated two-place USD decimal text and serialized as exact JSON number lexemes without floating-point conversion. Quantities retain up to six places. Journals must have one positive debit or credit per line, equal sides and a total equal to one side. Financial reads reject mismatching source references, amounts, accounts or parties rather than silently accepting a changed ledger document. QBO queries return complete lines; Xero invoice reference lookup requests a page to obtain line details.

Invoice and bill results expose normalized `open`, `partial` or `paid` status and two-place `paid`. Xero uses `AmountPaid` (credits are not cash payments) and preserves draft, void and deleted states. QBO uses `TotalAmt - Balance`, its net settled amount; this API field alone cannot distinguish credits from cash. Native QBO reconciliation separately reads exact Payment allocations and excludes linked zero-cash credit applications from cash. The QBO adapter can create a source-identified captured payment against an existing invoice, with its mapped clearing account; Xero payment writes remain unavailable. A receipt's `remoteId` is an **existing supplier bill ID**, and its attachment is UTF-8 evidence. `received: true` confirms attachment acceptance and visibility only; it does not settle a payable, confirm a physical receipt, or create another bill. QBO verifies filename, receipt key and bill link; Xero verifies filename and byte length within the supplied bill endpoint. Attachment metadata checks are not cryptographic content verification.

## Recovery and enablement boundary

Every QBO mutation uses `requestid`, a stable 48-hex-character SHA-256 prefix of `document.key`. Every Xero mutation uses `Idempotency-Key: document.key`. A key must identify one immutable operation, globally unique for that connection, and must never be reused for a changed body. [Intuit's request-ID guidance](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/learn/learn-basic-field-definitions#request-id) and [official API best practices](https://blogs.a.intuit.com/2018/09/10/quickbooks-online-api-best-practices/) describe request playback. [Xero's idempotency guide](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/idempotent-requests/idempotency/) documents its six-minute retention window. Provider idempotency is not durable application deduplication. A lost response requires persisted job identity and read and reconciliation; an absent lookup alone is not permission to create again after an uncertain write.

Reads return `null` only for an empty valid lookup or HTTP 404. Duplicate reference matches, malformed success responses and embedded validation failures throw. HTTP failures expose a `BooksProviderError` with `status`, while deliberately excluding raw response bodies and credentials. Redirects are refused. These adapters never retry a write automatically.

**QBO connections require explicit current-owner consent and reviewed company, item, party, account and cutover mappings.** The mapped USD tax-exempt subset now has live US sandbox evidence in `docs/proofs/qbo-sandbox-2026-10-26.json`; the fixture files themselves remain authored protocol examples. Xero still requires owner authorization and organization acceptance. Live period closure and authorization revocation, broader tax and channel settlements, real attachments and full uncertainty recovery remain acceptance gaps. Creating these fixtures used no account credentials and made no provider mutation.

## Official schema and example provenance

- QBO: [Invoice](https://developer.intuit.com/docs/api/accounting/invoice), [Item](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/api/accounting/all-entities/Item), [Bill](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/api/accounting/all-entities/bill), [JournalEntry](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/api/accounting/all-entities/journalentry), [Attachable](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/api/accounting/all-entities/attachable), [attachment workflow](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/workflows/attach-images-and-notes), and [official billing implementation](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/develop/basic-implementations/basic-billing-implementation).
- Xero: [Invoices](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/invoices), [Items](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/items), [Manual Journals](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/manualjournals), [Attachments](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/attachments/), [requests/responses](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/api/accounting/requests-and-responses/), and [official OpenAPI schema](https://github.com/XeroAPI/Xero-OpenAPI/blob/master/xero_accounting.yaml). The schema was also inspected directly for item fields and signed manual-journal lines when rendered documentation pages were unavailable.

The payloads retain documented field and envelope shapes but use newly authored values and omit unrelated optional fields. The fixture read exchanges deliberately change invoice and bill payment amounts to exercise reconciliation; they are authored transitions, not a recording of a ledger run.
